scope: Implemented P1 BFF technical boundary only; not environment or production release acceptance.
required_environment_followup: Upgrade affected installed runtime/SDK and migration package dependencies to the vendor-fixed 10.0.13 line or later approved stable patch, then rebuild/revalidate before production or identity activation.
exposure_analysis: No shipped BFF endpoint accepts XML, SignedXml, CMS/PKCS#7 or external certificates. The only shipped route is HTTPS health. Real sign-in is disabled and the default authoritative ticket store denies every identity.

Framework cryptographic operations remain framework-owned; BFF client input is protected cookie/antiforgery material, not caller-supplied XML/CMS. Data Protection key-ring and certificate custody are operator-controlled future deployment concerns.

Synthetic TLS tests import only their self-generated certificate. The current package audit identifies explicit vulnerable packages only in the unchanged migration project; it does not establish a clean installed shared runtime.

The new boundary has no unresolved demonstrated critical/high-risk attack path in its implemented transport scope. Vendor advisories remain OPEN environment/dependency findings; no risk acceptance, production clearance or immunity of shared framework is claimed.
threat_checks: HTTPS required; forwarded-header spoof does not upgrade HTTP
Explicit target host and Origin; no CORS or trusted proxy enabled
Secure/HttpOnly/host-only distinct cookie namespaces and Data Protection discriminators
Native server ticket storage; no browser principal/access/refresh token body
Deny-by-default store and disabled real sign-in; explicit expiry/no renewal
Explicit all-unsafe-verb and anonymous-endpoint antiforgery; duplicate/cross-surface header/token rejection
Existing safe Problem Details, server correlation, no-store/nosniff and redacted-only default logging
limitations: Owner restrictions/assurance/idle/rotation and authoritative store are later governed Identity/workforce work.
Technical component tests and Codex reviews do not constitute independent human security, release or production approval.
